issues.legal_issue: A tenant must initiate a dispute over standard rent within the prescribed notice period to prevent the strict arrears-based eviction provision from applying; raising the dispute for the first time later in the suit is insufficient.
material_facts: In one appeal, the tenants’ alleged letters disputing rent within the notice period were found to be manufactured, and a later letter was sent after that period.
In the other appeal, the tenants did not dispute standard rent within the notice period and first raised the dispute in their written statement.
The landlords’ claims concerned rent arrears, including arrears of at least six months, and the tenants had not made a timely application for fixation of standard rent.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that a tenant must raise the standard-rent dispute within one month after receiving the notice and apply to the court for fixation of standard rent within that period. A dispute first raised later in a written statement does not prevent application of the strict arrears-based eviction provision. The Court dismissed the Gujarat appeal and allowed the Bombay appeal, restoring the eviction decree in the latter.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 12(1), 12(2), and 12(3)(a) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, the strict eviction provision applies where monthly rent is at least six months in arrears, the tenant neglects to pay within the notice period, and there is no dispute about standard rent or permitted increases. Section 12(3)(b) governs other cases and provides protection subject to payment and continued tender of rent and costs. Explanation I to section 12 deems a tenant ready and willing to pay where, before expiry of one month after notice, the tenant applies under section 11(3) for fixation of standard rent and thereafter pays or tenders the amount specified by the court. Sections 11(3) and 11(4) govern interim orders in connection with a rent dispute, but are attracted only where the application disputing rent is made within the time contemplated by Explanation I. The Court applied Shah Dhansukhlal Chhanganlal v. Dalichand Virchand Shroff, and held that Vora Abbasbhai v. Haji Gulamnabi had not overruled the Gujarat High Court’s conclusion in Ambalal v. Badaldas that the dispute must exist no later than expiry of the one-month period.

predicates.rent_arrears_eviction_suit: A landlord brought a suit seeking eviction on the ground that the tenant had failed to pay rent.
predicates.dispute_first_raised_after_notice_deadli: The tenant first disputed the standard rent after the period for making the rent-fixation application had expired.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction for unpaid rent and the tenant first disputes standard rent only after the notice period, that late dispute does not prevent application of the strict eviction rule.
